answer: Each identity must lock a bond before it can trade at the wharf, and the deposit sits frozen while the agent works. Spawning clones costs real capital, so a thousand fake traders means a thousand bonds drained from one wallet. When the raven detects duplicate behavior across accounts, it slashes the bonds and pays the bounty to the reporter. A single garden of honest agents stays profitable, while sybil clusters bleed money faster than they can earn it back.
